item.title: Tennessee governor halts executions after Christa Gail Pike survives lethal injection
item.description: Tennessee officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death Wednesday for a 1995 murder after administering two doses of a lethal drug. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the remaining execution for the year.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
item.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Leaning into culture war flashpoints, Hegseth says he has transformed U.S. military
item.description: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told hundreds of junior military officers and enlisted leaders on Wednesday that the Trump administration has achieved a cultural shift in the military.

item.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

item.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong
item.description: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.

item.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting
item.description: The Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms that many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting.

item.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
item.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief, just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.

item.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
item.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.

item.title: On flight to Israel, pilot is stabbed, plane plunges before passengers tackle attacker
item.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, passengers and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.
